question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-6,-1],$ compute $P(Y>-5).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $Y$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le y\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-6,-1],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5},\, & -6\le y\le -1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>-5) & =P(-5<Y<-1) \\  & ={\int }_{-5}^{-1}f(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-5}^{-1}\frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{-1-(-5)}{5} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
